summary: James Henry Nelson was an Indologist. He earned an M.A. from the University of Cambridge in 1856 and served as a Fellow at King's College London.

James Hope Moulton worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Cambridge, London, and Edinburgh, learning under Edward Byles Cowell. He held posts at Didsbury College (1902) and the University of Manchester (1908).

James Irving Manatt was a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Grinnell and at Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held posts at Denison, Marietta, the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, and Brown University (~1892-1915).

James Ishmael Ford is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Sonoma State and the Pacific School of Religion, and trained under Mel Weitsman, Jiyu-Kennett, and John Tarrant. He founded Boundless Way Zen and Empty Moon Zen Network.

James Kennedy worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1859-1862). Kennedy served as a London Missionary Society missionary until 1877, lectured at University College London, and was treasurer of the Royal Asiatic Society (1904-1919).

James Kenneth Powell II is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Northwestern University, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD, 1998). His teachers included David Tracy, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.

James L. Fitzgerald works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Edwin Gerow, Edward Byles Cowell, and J. A. B. van Buitenen, earning a PhD from Chicago in 1980. He held professorships at the University of Tennessee and Brown University.

James L. Taylor is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Macquarie University in 1989 and served as Senior Lecturer in Anthropology at the University of Adelaide (attested 2014).

James Legge was a sinologist who studied at the University of Aberdeen and Highbury College. He served with the London Missionary Society (1839-1843), at the Anglo-Chinese College (1848-1873), and as a professor and fellow at the University of Oxford (1876-1897).

James Liddell Phillips was a linguistics and religious studies scholar. He was educated at Whitestown Seminary, Bowdoin College (graduating ~1860, D.D. 1878), and Columbia University Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons (M.D. ~1864).
James Long was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Church Missionary Society College, Islington, in 1838 and served as a missionary with the Church Mission Society beginning in 1840.
James Low works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and received traditional training under Chhimed Rigdzin Rinpoche.

James Luther Adams was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Minnesota, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University, later serving on the faculty at Harvard University from approximately 1957 to 1968.

James M. Macphail was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned an M.A. and M.D. from the University of Glasgow, founded the Bamdah Medical Mission in 1890, and served as a physician for the Free Church of Scotland (~1890-1929).

James Mackintosh was a scholar of history, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at the University of Aberdeen and University of Edinburgh, he founded and presided over the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1804-1811) and was a professor at East India Company College (1818-1824).

James Macnabb Campbell was an Indologist and historian. He was educated at The Glasgow Academy and the University of Glasgow (~1862-1866) and served in the Indian Civil Service from around 1869 to 1903.

Indologist James Mallinson studied at SOAS and the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at SOAS (2013) and Oxford (2023), where he became Boden Professor of Sanskrit and Director of Graduate Studies at Wolfson College.

James Mark Shields is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He has held faculty posts at Bucknell University (2007-2010, 2017) and served as an Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (attested 2016).
James Matthew Baskind is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at Yale University under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein (attested 2006).

Indology and religious studies scholar James McHugh studied at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard (PhD), supervised by Lawrence J. McCrea, Anne E. Monius, and Parimal G. Patil. He has held posts at Cornell University and the University of Southern California.
